==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=ParametersHashing&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Extensions/ParametersHashingTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=ParametersHashing&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
// Verify.ParametersHashing: Hashes test parameters into the snapshot file name with XxHash64, so large parameters cannot exceed path limits.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.ParametersHashing
// Note: This changes file *names*, not content. It has no converters, comparers or scrubbers.
// Note: VerifyParametersHashing.Initialize() registers nothing and only sets the initialized flag;
// the feature is entirely in the per verification HashParameters() call.
// Note: There is no global opt in: hashing is per verification.
// Note: The hash is the lowercase hex XxHash64 of the joined _name=value string, so changing a
// parameter renames its snapshot.
// Note: It replaces Verify's parameters appender, so it clashes with anything else that calls
// UseParametersAppender.
public class ParametersHashingTests
{
    // The snapshot file name normally ends in the stringified parameters, which can push the
    // path past what the OS allows. This appends an XxHash64 of them instead.
    // Add the test framework's parameterised attribute and a parameter to see it: the name then
    // ends in _25a91d2c54f27235 rather than in the value.
    [Fact]
    public Task HashParameters()
    {
        var settings = new VerifySettings();
        settings.HashParameters();
        return Verify("The target", settings);
    }

    // The fluent form does the same thing, for a test that does not already build a
    // VerifySettings of its own.
    [Fact]
    public Task HashParametersFluent()
    {
        return Verify("The target")
            .HashParameters();
    }
}
